current.text: Philadelphia traded for him from Boston this offseason, in the deal that sent Paul George away.
He is a projected starter next to Maxey, Edgecombe, LeBron James and Embiid.
Most experts expect his usage to fall from last season's 36% to about 27 to 30% because he shares the ball with Maxey, Embiid and LeBron. One expert still calls his usage in Philadelphia good.
Experts expect about four to five fewer points per game, with fewer assists and free throws. They expect him to have the biggest scoring drop of the Sixers stars.
Josh expects more rebounds and maybe a small gain in efficiency, and his projections still come out near 25 points, 7 rebounds and 4 assists.
His minutes should stay high or rise under Nick Nurse, maybe to 36 or 37 per game. That would partly offset the usage drop. His usage and minutes should rise when Embiid or LeBron sit.
He is expected to struggle more than LeBron to fit in at first. It is unclear whether he can play off the ball or do spot-up work, and the team expects growing pains in October and November.
Experts value him from about pick 37 to pick 52 (rounds 3 to 4). An ADP of 31 to 33 is a little rich, a pick in the 20s is too early, and pick 52 is too late. One category ranking has him near 35.
In an auction mock, 23 USD was called a good price for him.
Yahoo lists him as questionable for rest.
Philadelphia plays 3, 4 and 4 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has only 13 back-to-backs all season. One note says three of those back-to-backs fall in the fantasy playoffs.
Philadelphia is projected to win about 51 to 52 games, with some load management for its stars.
The Sixers bench is weak, so the starters should carry heavy loads.

durable.text: Turnovers are his one clear weak category. At about 2.9 per game projected, he is a league outlier for turnovers.

Scoring is his main fantasy category. Experts disagree on the rest. One sees solid rebounds, assists, steals and threes, with percentages that do not hurt. Others say he gives little beyond scoring and rebounds, or beyond scoring alone.
Plain nine-cat rankings underrate what he gives in head-to-head category leagues.
He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues. Last season he was about 10th in points leagues and about 25th in category leagues.
Experts disagree on his defense. Josh calls it a little overrated, and Mark calls him a more than solid defender.

note: Experts see him as a round 3 to 4 player in category leagues (picks about 37 to 52). Yahoo's average cost is 24 USD and ESPN's is 20 USD, and a mock price of 23 USD was called good, so 20 to 24 USD is fair. Last season's 29 USD in our league was paid for a 36% usage role he no longer has. Turnovers are his only real weakness, so he fits best in a punt TO build. Early on, check his usage and his minutes (36 or more is the hope), how often Embiid and LeBron sit, and whether the expected October-November growing pains hold down his scoring.
